(CNN) -- After encountering numerous black couples in crisis, Nisa Muhammad and Dr. Rozario Slack were inspired to create Basic Training for Couples. Nisa Muhammad, the founder of National Black Marriage Day, co-created the Basic Training for Couples program. This eight-week program educates dating, engaged, and married couples about the value of commitment, responsibility to the black community, the psychological differences between the sexes, sexual intimacy, and conflict resolution. Slack developed the male-friendly component, while Muhammad, who founded both National Black Marriage Day and the Wedded Bliss Foundation, designed the female-friendly component. Throughout the program, couples also explore the history of African-American marriage, and many, for the first time, chart their own family tree to trace marriages and divorces across generations.

The following is an overview of the eight-week course:

**Class No. 1: Why Marriage?**
This class examines the benefits of marriage for men, women, children, and the community. It traces the history of marriage within the black community, from the era of slavery—when marriage was illegal—to present-day trends.
Icebreaker: A question-and-answer session on how couples met.
Homework:
1. Select songs that reflect their love for each other.
2. Complete their marriage family tree.

**Class No. 2: From I to We; the Sweetness of Surrender**
This class helps couples transition from "I thinking" to "we thinking." It fosters an understanding of the value of making their marriage a priority in their lives.

**Class No. 3: Communication; Getting Your Message Understood**
This class encourages couples to take responsibility for their communication and teaches skills to enhance their communication techniques.
Main lessons:
• Respecting the differences between men and women
• Learning to talk to each other rather than at each other
• Format: A teaching session with guided dialogue.
• Activity: The talking stick, in which only the individual holding the stick may speak during conversation.

**Class No. 4: Conflict Management**
This class helps couples understand that conflict must be managed, or it will manage them. It works to normalize some of the conflict couples experience, with the recognition that certain conflicts cannot be resolved and can only be managed.
Lessons:
• This class addresses biases. When a difference of opinion arises, the more dominant spouse typically wants his or her own way.
• How to bring closure to old issues instead of allowing them to compound into new conflicts.
• Agreeing to disagree without degrading one's spouse for holding a differing opinion.
Activity: Dividing into gender groups to discuss current conflicts, with each group working out ways to resolve the issue.

**Class No. 5: Let's Make Love**
When the sex is good in a marriage, it accounts for only about 20 percent of what is going on; when it is bad, it becomes a significant problem. This class helps to resolve some of those problems, approaching the subject from a physiological and biological perspective on the differences between the male and female body. The discussion includes the chemical bonding effect in both women and men.

**Class No. 6: From Yours and Mine to Ours**
Many couples in the black community bring children from previous relationships into their marriage. This class helps to blend the family into one cohesive unit. It also addresses how to prevent in-laws from becoming outlaws.

**Class No. 7: Keeping the FIRE Burning**
FIRE is an acronym for Faithful, Intimacy, Responsibility, and Excitement. This class helps couples maintain the FIRE in their relationship.

**Class No. 8: From This Day Forward**
This class helps couples appreciate the value of commitment in their marriage and to never regard divorce as an option. Together, they create their own foundation for success.
A recap of all the lessons:
• Remembering that people gravitate toward applause
• Ways to appreciate and affirm one's spouse
• Setting aside time for just the two of them
• Learning to communicate—getting one's message heard and understood

**Bonus Class: Hot Monogamy**
This class helps couples grow comfortable discussing sex with their spouse.

**Graduation**
A ceremony marking new beginnings, in which couples testify to what the class has brought to their marriage over the eight-week period. This is a time of profound emotion and bonding between husbands and wives. Graduating couples are encouraged to bring along a couple from their community or family who is in need of help.

(CNN) -- When Nisa Muhammad and Dr. Rozario Slack encountered several African-American couples struggling in their relationships, the experience motivated them to develop a program called Basic Training for Couples. Muhammad, the person behind National Black Marriage Day, helped bring this initiative to life alongside Slack.

Spanning two months, the curriculum instructs couples—whether they're dating, engaged, or already wed—on topics such as the importance of commitment, duty toward the black community, the mental and emotional distinctions between men and women, physical closeness, and how to handle disagreements. Slack developed the sections geared toward men, whereas Muhammad, who established both National Black Marriage Day and the Wedded Bliss Foundation, designed the material aimed at women. Participants also study how African-American marriage has evolved over time, and for many, the program marks the first occasion they map out a family tree documenting unions and separations across generations.

Here's a breakdown of the eight-week curriculum:

**Session 1: Why marriage?**
This opening lesson highlights the advantages marriage offers to men, women, kids, and society at large. It traces marriage within the black community back to the era of slavery, when such unions were forbidden, up through modern-day patterns. Icebreaker: A question-and-answer exchange about how each couple first crossed paths. Assignments: 1) Pick songs that capture their affection for one another. 2) Build their marriage family tree.

**Session 2: From I to we; the sweetness of surrender**
Here, couples work on shifting away from thinking as individuals toward thinking as partners. The lesson underscores why placing their marriage at the center of their lives matters.

**Session 3: Communication; getting your message understood**
This class encourages couples to own their communication styles and offers techniques for improving how they interact. Key takeaways include respecting male-female differences and learning to speak with one another rather than at each other. The format combines instruction with conversation. Activity: The talking stick—only the partner holding it is permitted to speak during dialogue.

**Session 4: Conflict management**
The message here is that couples must control conflict, or it will end up controlling them. The class reassures partners that friction is normal while explaining that certain disputes can't be fixed—only managed. Lessons cover: addressing personal biases, since the more dominant partner often insists on getting their way during disagreements; wrapping up lingering issues rather than piling them onto fresh ones; and agreeing to disagree without belittling a partner for holding a different view. Activity: Splitting into separate groups by gender to talk through ongoing conflicts and brainstorm solutions.

**Session 5: Let's make love**
A satisfying sex life accounts for roughly 20 percent of a marriage, but poor intimacy becomes a major issue. This lesson tackles some of those difficulties, examining the biological and physiological contrasts between male and female bodies. Discussion touches on how chemical bonding differs between the sexes.

**Session 6: From yours and mine to ours**
Numerous couples in the black community enter marriage with children from prior relationships. This session focuses on merging everyone into a single, unified family while also addressing how to keep in-laws from turning into adversaries.

**Session 7: Keeping the FIRE burning**
FIRE stands for Faithful, Intimacy, Responsibility, and Excitement. This lesson guides couples in sustaining that FIRE within their partnership.

**Session 8: From this day forward**
The final class reinforces the importance of staying committed and treating divorce as off the table. Couples craft their own blueprint for a thriving relationship. The session reviews all prior lessons, emphasizing: how people are drawn to praise, ways to value and reassure a partner, carving out time exclusively for the two of them, and mastering communication so messages are truly heard and understood.

**Bonus session: Hot monogamy**
This lesson helps partners feel at ease talking openly about sex with each other.

**Graduation**
Framed as a celebration of fresh starts, graduating couples share how the eight-week experience transformed their marriage. The occasion is filled with strong emotion and deepened connection between spouses. Those completing the program are urged to bring along another couple—from their family or neighborhood—who could benefit from the same help.

The program teaches the history of African-American marriage, tracing its evolution from a period when such unions were illegal during slavery to the modern trends that shape relationships today. # Basic Training for Couples: Strengthening African-American Relationships

The inspiration for Basic Training for Couples emerged from real encounters with black couples navigating difficult times in their relationships. Nisa Muhammad and Dr. Rozario Slack, witnessing the struggles these couples faced, recognized a pressing need for a structured approach to relationship education tailored specifically to the African-American experience. Their response was to create a comprehensive program designed to equip couples with the tools they need to build lasting, healthy partnerships.

## An Eight-Week Journey

The program they developed spans eight weeks and takes a gender-tailored approach, acknowledging that men and women often experience and communicate within relationships differently. Rather than offering a one-size-fits-all curriculum, Basic Training for Couples addresses the distinct perspectives and needs that partners bring to their union.

The program welcomes couples at various stages of their relationships—those who are dating and exploring their compatibility, those who are engaged and preparing for marriage, and those who are already married and seeking to strengthen their bond. This inclusive design ensures that couples can benefit from the curriculum regardless of where they stand in their journey together.

## A Comprehensive Curriculum

The content of Basic Training for Couples covers a broad range of essential relationship topics. Participants explore the foundations of **commitment**, learning what it means to fully invest in a partnership. They develop **communication** skills that allow them to express themselves clearly and listen to their partners effectively. The program also addresses **sexual intimacy**, helping couples cultivate closeness and understanding in this important dimension of their relationship.

**Conflict resolution** forms another key component, giving couples practical strategies for navigating disagreements in constructive ways. Perhaps most distinctively, the curriculum incorporates the **history of African-American marriage**, providing cultural and historical context that helps couples understand and appreciate the significance of marriage within their community.

## Interactive Learning

What sets Basic Training for Couples apart is its emphasis on hands-on, interactive learning. Rather than relying solely on lectures or reading materials, the program engages participants through meaningful activities. Couples plot their **family trees**, connecting their present relationships to their broader family histories and legacies. The program also employs a **"talking stick,"** a tool that structures conversation by giving each partner a designated opportunity to speak while the other listens—fostering respect and reducing interruptions during important discussions.

## A Larger Mission

Beyond helping individual couples, Basic Training for Couples carries a broader purpose. The program aims to strengthen relationships and reinforce the value of marriage within the black community. By combining practical relationship skills with cultural awareness and historical understanding, Muhammad and Slack created a resource that not only supports couples in crisis but also celebrates and promotes the enduring importance of committed partnerships among African-Americans.

# After the Broadcast

Nisa had always been the quiet one in her family, content to observe rather than participate. But everything changed the evening she watched a particular segment on **CNN**.

The report focused on young entrepreneurs who had built successful businesses from nothing. Nisa sat frozen on her couch, watching a woman not much older than herself describe the moment she decided to stop waiting for the perfect opportunity and simply began.

**After** the program ended, Nisa couldn't shake the feeling that something inside her had shifted. She had spent years dreaming about opening her own small bakery, jotting recipes into notebooks and imagining the smell of fresh bread filling a shop that existed only in her mind.

That night, Nisa made a decision. She pulled out her old business plan, dusted off the numbers, and began to rework them with fresh determination. The story she had seen on **CNN** proved that ordinary people could accomplish extraordinary things when they refused to give up.

The weeks that followed were far from easy. Nisa faced rejection from banks, doubts from relatives, and countless sleepless nights. Yet each time discouragement crept in, she remembered the courage of the entrepreneur on television.

**After** eighteen months of relentless effort, Nisa finally unlocked the door to her very own bakery. Standing behind the counter on opening day, watching customers smile at their first bite, she realized that a single moment of inspiration had changed the entire course of her life.

Sometimes, all it takes is one story to spark a lifetime of change.

# Building Stronger Marriages: Inside the "Basic Training for Couples" Program

*A relationship education initiative aims to give couples practical tools for lasting commitment*

Marriage takes work—and according to relationship educators Nisa Muhammad and Dr. Rozario Slack, it also takes training. The two developed "Basic Training for Couples," an eight-week program designed to help couples build the skills needed for healthy, lasting relationships.

The program has been used in community settings, faith-based organizations, and relationship education workshops as part of a broader movement to strengthen marriages through practical, skills-based education rather than relying on romance alone.

## A Skills-Based Approach to Love

The philosophy behind Basic Training for Couples is straightforward: just as people train for careers and other life pursuits, they can also learn the skills that make marriages thrive. The curriculum focuses on communication, conflict resolution, expectations, and shared values.

Here's a look at the structure of the eight-week program:

### Week 1: Getting to Know You
The opening session focuses on building a foundation of understanding. Couples explore each other's backgrounds, family histories, and personal expectations. The goal is to establish honest communication early and identify what each partner brings into the relationship.

### Week 2: Communication
This week centers on the cornerstone of any strong relationship: effective communication. Couples learn to express themselves clearly, listen actively, and understand the difference between hearing and truly listening to a partner.

### Week 3: Conflict Resolution
Recognizing that disagreements are inevitable, this session teaches couples how to handle conflict constructively. Participants learn to fight fair, avoid destructive patterns, and work toward resolutions that respect both partners.

### Week 4: Forgiveness
Week four addresses the importance of forgiveness in sustaining a relationship. Couples explore how holding onto resentment can erode a partnership and learn strategies for letting go of past hurts to move forward together.

### Week 5: Finances
Money is a frequent source of marital tension. This week helps couples discuss financial goals, spending habits, and budgeting. The aim is to get partners on the same page about money before it becomes a source of conflict.

### Week 6: Intimacy
This session explores intimacy in its many forms—emotional, physical, and spiritual. Couples learn how to nurture closeness and maintain connection throughout the different seasons of a relationship.

### Week 7: Roles and Expectations
Week seven examines the roles each partner plays and the expectations they hold. Couples work to clarify responsibilities and align their visions for the partnership, reducing misunderstandings that can arise from unspoken assumptions.

### Week 8: Commitment
The final week ties everything together with a focus on commitment. Couples reflect on what they've learned and reaffirm their dedication to building a lasting relationship, equipped with the tools introduced throughout the program.

## Part of a Larger Movement

Nisa Muhammad, a longtime advocate for marriage and family, has been known for founding initiatives promoting healthy relationships, including efforts encouraging marriage awareness in communities. Dr. Rozario Slack, a relationship educator and speaker, has worked extensively in the field of marriage and family strengthening.

Together, their program reflects a growing emphasis among relationship educators on prevention—giving couples skills before problems escalate—rather than intervention after difficulties arise.

Supporters of programs like Basic Training for Couples argue that relationship education can benefit not just individual couples but entire communities, contributing to family stability and stronger social bonds.

For couples considering the program, the message from its creators is clear: a great marriage isn't just something you find—it's something you build.

---

*Note: For the most current information on program availability and enrollment, couples should consult official program sources or affiliated organizations.*

# Building Strong Bonds: A Marriage Education Program

## Program Overview

**Building Strong Bonds** is a culturally-responsive marriage education program designed to strengthen relationships within the African-American community. The program acknowledges the unique historical, cultural, and social contexts that shape Black marriages while celebrating the resilience, faith traditions, and community values that serve as sources of strength.

### Guiding Principles

- **Cultural affirmation**: Honoring African-American heritage, extended family structures, and community bonds
- **Faith-inclusive**: Welcoming (but not requiring) the spiritual traditions central to many families
- **Strengths-based**: Building on existing relationship assets rather than focusing solely on deficits
- **Contextually aware**: Addressing external stressors like economic pressures and systemic challenges
- **Community-centered**: Recognizing "it takes a village" support systems

### Format

- 10 weekly sessions, 2 hours each
- Small group setting (6–8 couples)
- Facilitated by trained leaders who reflect the community
- Includes shared meals, take-home exercises, and mentor-couple pairings

---

## Week-by-Week Course Outline

### Week 1: Foundations — Our Story, Our Legacy
- Welcome, program overview, and group agreements
- Exploring personal and family relationship histories
- Understanding the strengths and challenges of Black marriage in historical context
- **Couple activity**: Sharing your love story and family relationship legacies
- **Takeaway**: Vision statement for your marriage

### Week 2: Communication — Hearing and Being Heard
- Foundations of healthy communication
- Speaker-Listener techniques and active listening
- Recognizing communication patterns learned in family of origin
- Navigating cultural expressions of emotion and directness
- **Couple activity**: Practicing reflective listening exercises
- **Takeaway**: Daily 15-minute check-in practice

### Week 3: Understanding Each Other — Differences and Expectations
- Uncovering assumptions and unspoken expectations
- Gender roles and evolving partnership dynamics
- Balancing individual identity within the marriage
- **Couple activity**: Expectations inventory and discussion
- **Takeaway**: Mapping shared and individual needs

### Week 4: Managing Conflict — Fighting Fair
- Understanding sources of conflict and escalation
- Identifying destructive patterns (criticism, defensiveness, stonewalling)
- Time-outs and de-escalation strategies
- Addressing external stressors that fuel conflict
- **Couple activity**: Practicing a structured problem-solving model
- **Takeaway**: Personalized "rules of engagement"

### Week 5: Forgiveness and Healing
- The role of forgiveness in lasting relationships
- Repairing after conflict and rebuilding trust
- Healing from past hurts, including generational wounds
- Faith and community as resources for restoration
- **Couple activity**: Guided forgiveness conversation
- **Takeaway**: Personal reflection on areas needing healing

### Week 6: Intimacy and Connection — Emotional Closeness
- Building and maintaining emotional intimacy
- Vulnerability, safety, and trust
- Rekindling friendship and appreciation
- Overcoming barriers to closeness (stress, busyness, past experiences)
- **Couple activity**: Love map and appreciation exercise
- **Takeaway**: Weekly connection ritual

### Week 7: Physical Intimacy and Romance
- Nurturing physical and sexual intimacy
- Communicating desires and needs respectfully
- Keeping romance alive across life stages
- Addressing cultural messages about intimacy
- **Couple activity**: Private discussion guide for partners
- **Takeaway**: Planning intentional romance and quality time

### Week 8: Finances, Stress, and Partnership
- Working as a financial team
- Managing economic pressures and building stability
- Navigating debt, saving, and shared goals
- Stress management and mutual support
- **Couple activity**: Creating a shared budget and money values discussion
- **Takeaway**: Financial goal-setting worksheet

### Week 9: Family, Community, and Parenting
- Managing extended family relationships and boundaries
- Co-parenting as a united team
- Passing on values to the next generation
- Leveraging community and church support networks
- **Couple activity**: Defining your family's values and boundaries
- **Takeaway**: Identifying your support "village"

### Week 10: Commitment — Building a Lasting Legacy
- The meaning and practice of lifelong commitment
- Renewing dedication in difficult seasons
- Creating a long-term relationship maintenance plan
- Connecting with mentor couples and ongoing support
- **Couple activity**: Commitment ceremony and vow renewal
- **Celebration**: Graduation, testimonies, and community meal
- **Takeaway**: Ongoing "marriage maintenance" plan and mentor connection

---

## Ongoing Support Components

- **Mentor couples**: Established couples paired with participants for continued guidance
- **Alumni gatherings**: Quarterly reunions to sustain community
- **Booster sessions**: Refresher workshops at 6 and 12 months
- **Resource referrals**: Connections to counseling, financial, and faith-based resources

---

**Note**: For real-world implementation, consider partnering with established, evidence-informed frameworks and evaluating outcomes. Programs are strengthened by input from local community leaders, clergy, and participating couples to ensure cultural authenticity and relevance.

Would you like me to expand any particular week into a detailed session plan, or develop facilitator guides and participant handouts?

# Eight-Week Marriage Counseling Curriculum for Black Couples

## Program Overview

This culturally-affirming curriculum honors the historical strengths, spiritual traditions, and communal values within Black relationships while addressing the unique pressures couples may face. Each session integrates evidence-based counseling techniques with cultural relevance.

---

## Week 1: "Rooted in Love — Understanding Our Foundation"

**Lesson Focus:** Exploring individual and shared histories, family patterns, and relationship expectations.

**Activities:**
- Genogram exercise mapping relationship patterns across generations
- "Our Love Story" timeline where couples recount how they met
- Group discussion on cultural values that shaped their views of marriage

**Homework:** Interview an elder or family member about their marriage lessons; journal one strength each partner brings to the relationship.

---

## Week 2: "Speaking Our Truth — Communication That Heals"

**Lesson Focus:** Active listening, expressing needs, and avoiding destructive patterns.

**Activities:**
- Role-play using "I" statements
- The "Listener/Speaker" exercise with reflective feedback
- Identifying communication styles inherited from family of origin

**Homework:** Practice a daily 15-minute "check-in" with no phones; complete a communication self-assessment.

---

## Week 3: "Navigating the World Together — Stress, Race, and Resilience"

**Lesson Focus:** Addressing external stressors including racial trauma, economic pressure, and discrimination as a united front.

**Activities:**
- Discussion on how outside stress enters the home ("weathering")
- Building a "resilience toolkit" as a couple
- Identifying how to be a safe harbor for one another

**Homework:** Create a shared plan for supporting each other during difficult external situations.

---

## Week 4: "Managing the Money — Financial Partnership"

## Week 7: "Building Our Village — Family, Community, and Boundaries"

## Week 8: "Legacy of Love — Vision and Celebration"

# Celebrating Love and Commitment: The Legacy of National Black Marriage Day

## How Nisa Muhammad Built a Movement to Strengthen Marriages in the Black Community

For more than two decades, Nisa Islam Muhammad has championed a cause close to her heart: strengthening marriages and families within the Black community. As the founder of National Black Marriage Day, she has helped transform a simple observance into a nationwide celebration of love, commitment, and family stability.

---

## The Founder's Journey

Nisa Muhammad is a marriage educator, journalist, and family advocate who recognized a pressing need in her community. Working as a staff writer and observing declining marriage rates and rising rates of single-parent households in Black America, she felt called to action. Rather than simply documenting these trends, Muhammad decided to become part of the solution.

In 2003, she founded the **Wedded Bliss Foundation**, a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting healthy marriages and relationships. Through this platform, she launched initiatives designed to provide practical relationship education and to reframe cultural conversations around marriage.

---

## The Birth of National Black Marriage Day

National Black Marriage Day was established in 2003 and is observed annually on the **fourth Sunday in March**. The observance was created to celebrate and encourage marriage in the Black community while countering negative narratives about Black relationships and family life.

The day has grown from a modest observance into a coast-to-coast celebration, with communities, churches, and organizations hosting events including:

- Marriage celebrations and vow renewals
- Educational workshops and seminars
- Community dinners and gatherings
- Recognition ceremonies for long-married couples
- Panel discussions on relationship wellness

The initiative has been recognized in cities across the United States, with local proclamations and events drawing participation from faith communities, civic organizations, and families.

---

## Basic Training for Couples

Among Muhammad's most significant contributions is the **Basic Training for Couples** program, a relationship education curriculum designed to give couples practical tools for building strong, lasting partnerships.

### Program Philosophy

The program operates on the principle that successful marriages require skills that can be taught and learned—not merely luck or chemistry. Drawing on evidence-based relationship education models, Basic Training for Couples aims to equip couples with communication techniques, conflict-resolution strategies, and a deeper understanding of partnership dynamics.

---

## A Note on the Syllabus

I want to be transparent: I don't have verified access to the complete, official syllabus for Muhammad's specific "Basic Training for Couples" curriculum, and I don't want to fabricate the exact proprietary contents she developed. Below, I've outlined a **representative syllabus** based on common structures in evidence-based marriage education programs, clearly labeled as illustrative. For the authentic, complete curriculum, I'd recommend contacting the Wedded Bliss Foundation directly.

---

## Representative Program Syllabus (Illustrative Framework)

**Format:** Typically delivered over 6–8 weekly sessions

### Session 1: Foundations of Partnership
- Understanding expectations and marriage myths
- Sharing individual visions for the relationship
- Establishing shared goals and values

### Session 2: Communication Skills
- Active and reflective listening techniques
- Speaking to be understood
- Recognizing communication barriers

### Session 3: Conflict Resolution
- Understanding healthy vs. unhealthy conflict
- De-escalation strategies
- Fair-fighting rules and repair techniques

### Session 4: Finances and Household Management
- Aligning financial goals
- Budgeting and money conversations
- Dividing responsibilities

### Session 5: Intimacy and Connection
- Emotional and physical intimacy
- Maintaining friendship and romance
- Understanding love languages

### Session 6: Family and Community
- Navigating extended family relationships
- Parenting philosophies and co-parenting
- Building a support network

### Session 7: Faith and Values (where applicable)
- Shared spiritual practices
- Values-based decision making
- Purpose-driven partnership

### Session 8: Commitment and the Road Ahead
- Renewing commitment
- Creating a relationship action plan
- Ongoing growth and resources

---

## A Lasting Impact

Through National Black Marriage Day and programs like Basic Training for Couples, Nisa Muhammad has helped shift cultural conversations and provided tangible support to countless couples. Her work underscores a powerful message: that marriage is worth celebrating, worth working for, and worth investing in.

As the observance continues each March, Muhammad's legacy endures in every couple who gains the tools and encouragement to build a stronger union.

---

# Faith-Based Relationship Enrichment Program

## "Two Becoming One: Building Relationships on Sacred Ground"

Here's a comprehensive multi-session program designed for couples at various stages. This works well as a 10-week core program with bonus sessions.

---

## Core Program Structure

### **Session 1: Foundations — Faith at the Center**
**Icebreaker:** "Three Truths" — Each partner shares three things that first attracted them to the other, including one faith-related quality.

**Content:**
- Establishing a shared spiritual vision for the relationship
- The concept of a "three-strand cord" (partner, partner, and faith)
- Setting group covenant/confidentiality expectations
- Discussion: What does a faith-centered relationship mean to each of you?

**Takeaway:** Couples write a shared "mission statement" for their relationship.

---

### **Session 2: Communication as a Sacred Practice**
**Icebreaker:** "Mirror Me" — Partners take turns describing their day while the other listens and reflects back without adding commentary.

**Content:**
- Active listening and speaking with grace
- The difference between hearing and understanding
- Scriptural/spiritual principles on the power of words
- Communication styles inventory

**Takeaway:** Practice a "daily check-in" ritual at home.

---

### **Session 3: Understanding Conflict & Forgiveness**
**Icebreaker:** "Weather Report" — Each partner describes their current emotional "weather" (sunny, stormy, etc.).

**Content:**
- Healthy vs. unhealthy conflict patterns
- The role of forgiveness and reconciliation in faith traditions
- Repair attempts and de-escalation
- Distinguishing between forgiveness and accountability

**Takeaway:** Identify one recurring conflict pattern to address together.

---

### **Session 4: Love Languages & Serving One Another**
**Icebreaker:** "Gift Memory" — Recall a moment your partner made you feel deeply loved.

**Content:**
- Exploring the five love languages
- Servant-hearted love as a spiritual discipline
- Meeting needs vs. wants
- Practical acts of daily devotion to each other

**Takeaway:** Commit to speaking your partner's primary love language this week.

---

### **Session 5: Roles, Expectations & Partnership**
**Icebreaker:** "Family Snapshot" — Share one thing you loved and one thing you'd change from the home you grew up in.

**Content:**
- Examining inherited beliefs about relationship roles
- Building mutual respect and shared decision-making
- Navigating differing expectations with grace
- Faith perspectives on partnership and mutual submission

**Takeaway:** List three expectations you've never voiced to your partner.

---

### **Session 6: Finances & Stewardship**
**Icebreaker:** "Money Memory" — What's your earliest memory involving money?

**Content:**
- Money as a spiritual and practical issue
- Budgeting, generosity, and financial transparency
- Debt, saving, and shared goals
- Principles of stewardship and contentment

**Takeaway:** Schedule a monthly "money date."

---

### **Session 7: Intimacy & Physical Connection**
*(Tailor content by group stage: dating, engaged, married)*

**Icebreaker:** "Comfort Zones" — Share a non-physical way your partner makes you feel safe.

**Content:**
- Emotional, physical, and spiritual intimacy
- Healthy boundaries appropriate to relationship stage
- Faith perspectives on sexuality and commitment
- Rebuilding connection and vulnerability

**Takeaway:** Discuss what makes each of you feel emotionally safe.

---

### **Session 8: Family, In-Laws & Community**
**Icebreaker:** "The Village" — Name one person who has strengthened your relationship.

**Content:**
- Leaving and cleaving: establishing your own household
- Setting healthy boundaries with extended family
- Building a supportive community around your relationship
- Handling holidays and family traditions

**Takeaway:** Identify a mentor couple you both admire.

---

### **Session 9: Vision, Purpose & Legacy**
**Icebreaker:** "Ten Years From Now" — Describe your ideal ordinary Tuesday a decade from now.

**Content:**
- Aligning individual and shared purpose
- Discerning calling as a couple
- Children, ministry, and service (as applicable)
- Building a lasting spiritual legacy

**Takeaway:** Draft a shared five-year vision.

---

### **Session 10: Covenant & Celebration**
**Icebreaker:** "Growth Reflection" — Share one thing you've learned about your partner during this program.

**Content:**
- Reviewing key lessons and commitments
- The meaning of covenant vs. contract
- Renewing or making commitments to one another
- Celebration meal and blessing

**Takeaway:** A written recommitment or covenant statement, and a plan for ongoing growth.

---

## Bonus Sessions

### **Bonus A: Praying & Worshiping Together**
Practical guidance on building shared spiritual practices — devotionals, prayer, and worship as a couple, tailored to comfort levels.

### **Bonus B: Weathering Life's Storms**
Navigating crisis, grief, illness, job loss, and infertility with faith and resilience. Building a "storm plan" together.

### **Bonus C: Blended Families & Second Marriages**
Special considerations for stepparenting, ex-spouse relationships, and honoring past chapters while building anew.

### **Bonus D: Technology, Boundaries & Trust**
Healthy digital habits, social media, and guarding against outside intrusions on the relationship.

### **Bonus E: Couples' Retreat Day**
A half-day intensive combining reflection, worship, guided conversation stations, and a renewal ceremony.

---

## Facilitation Tips

- **Group size:** 4–8 couples for meaningful discussion
- **Format:** 90–120 minutes per session with mingling time
- **Materials:** Provide couple workbooks/journals
- **Table setup:** Couples sit together; mix groups for large-group discussion
- **Leadership:** Ideally co-facilitated by a mentor couple
- **Follow-up:** Pair couples with mentor couples for post-program support
